description:
FILED s399 (user, at session end): "that one hour sweep can't be run every half
hour".  Correct, and the fix is not discipline — it is that the run spends most
of its wall time on files ALREADY KNOWN to be hung or crawling.

WHERE THE HOUR GOES (measured s399, `--all --jobs 4 --timeout 300`):
  * the six re/regexp*.t + re/overload.t known-HANG files (task #326) burn the
    full per-file timeout each — at 300 s that is ~30 min of CPU, ~7.5 min of
    wall at 4 jobs, and they produce NOTHING;
  * re/pat_psycho.t (>400 s) and re/speed.t, which since s399j RUN the
    pathological patterns instead of dying early (task #324) — another ~10 min
    of CPU for ~12 rows;
  * comp/require.t 450 s and re/pat_advanced.t 900 s are registered allowances
    that genuinely earn their time (909 and 936 rows).
So roughly HALF the run is the known-bad tail, and it is the same tail every
time.

PROPOSAL (sizing, not designed):
  1. `--quick` / `--skip-known-hangs`: skip the files whose ONLY measured
     outcome is TIMEOUT-with-no-rows (the #326 set), the way op/list.t and
     op/pack.t are already QUARANTINED.  They must still be listed in the
     report as NOT-RUN so the coverage hole stays visible — never silently.
     Expected: a full run in roughly half the wall time, with identical
     information.
  2. A per-file allowance CAP in quick mode (e.g. min(row, 120 s)), so a
     registered-slow file contributes what it can rather than its full budget.
  3. Then state the CADENCE in CLAUDE.md explicitly, because today it is
     implicit and I over-ran it:
       - per change: gate + corpus-diff (+ the targeted files the change can
         touch).  corpus-diff identical AND no cl/ or lib/ or perl-tests/t/
         change AND not a name-resolution change ⇒ the full perl-tests sweep
         CANNOT move: skip it, do not "run it to be safe".
       - full perl-tests sweep: when one of those triggers fires (a runtime or
         shim change is invisible to corpus-diff), else every 3rd–5th change.
       - companion `--all`: at most once per session, and only for a change
         that can move files corpus-diff cannot see (a harness change like
         s399j, or a name-resolution change).  Otherwise run the DIRS the
         change touches.
MEASURED JUSTIFICATION for rule 3's negative: of s399's four full sweeps, two
(#332, #314 F-D) followed an IDENTICAL corpus-diff and found exactly nothing —
~20 minutes that the rule above would have saved without weakening any bar.

BAR: `--quick` must print what it skipped and why, and one `--all` vs
`--all --quick` comparison must show the same verdicts for every file that
runs in both.


RULED s401 (docs/fable-answers-s400.md Â§8): the count rule is RETIRED; the
WHAT-CHANGED decision table is in CLAUDE.md (Quick Reference, "WHAT TO RUN
WHEN") â implement, do not re-derive.  Proposal items 1 + 2 APPROVED
(`--quick` = default companion form: skip the #326 hang set, cap registered
allowances at 120 s, LIST every skipped/capped file as NOT-RUN).  Also
register re/pat_psycho.t + re/speed.t in docs/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv (their
12 rows are real; the full run that pays for them is now rare).  BAR as
filed: prints what it skipped and why; one --all vs --all --quick comparison
shows identical verdicts for every file that runs in both.  Session B of
docs/plan-post-s400.md.


DONE s404 (commit 00b150f).  `--quick` implemented: %QUICK_SKIP (the measured
hang set) + a 120 s cap on registered allowances; every skipped/capped file
gets a NOT-RUN row naming the rule and its cause, counting as UNEXPLAINED
like QUARANTINE.  DEVIATION from proposal item 2, deliberate: a capped file
is NOT run on a smaller budget (a truncated TAP stream is a different
measurement, and it would break the bar).

MEASURED at 90/300/900 s: re/overload.t 3 of 87 rows at all three and
re/speed.t 1 of 59 at 300 and 900 -> HANGS, skip set; re/pat_psycho.t
COMPLETED at 300 s with 11 rows -> SLOW, registered 450 s in
docs/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv (so the cap keeps it out of quick anyway).  That
is why s400 §7.4 held for one of its two files and not the other.

BAR MET: --all vs --all --quick on the same tree -> 512 files ran in both,
510 identical in verdict AND counts; the 2 others are the *rows-unstable*
file and op/utf8cache.t (TIMEOUT vs DIFF at identical 2/0 counts).  All 9
skipped files came back TIMEOUT in the full run.  Wall 13 min vs 19.5 min at
--jobs 4.
subject: The companion --all run costs an hour and HALF of it is the known-hang tail: a --quick mode + a written cadence rule (user, s399)
